newsitem.title: DENMARK: Sun-Air buys three aircraft from British Aerospace.
newsitem.headline: Sun-Air buys three aircraft from British Aerospace.

text.p: Danish short-haul carrier Sun-Air of Scandinavia said on Tuesday that it had agreed to buy two British Aerospace Advanced Turbo-Prop aircraft and one Jetstream 41.
A Sun-Air statement said that the purchase was due to increased passenger volume resulting from its British Airways Express franchise, inaugurated in August 1996.
"Co-operation with British Airways has given us a marked increase in passenger numbers which we wish to strengthen by investing in higher capacity on our routes," it said.
Sun-Air did not give the purchase price for the new planes.

It said that one of the Advanced Turbo-Props would go into service on flights between the western Danish airport of Billund and Manchester in Britain, Billund and the Norwegian caiptal, Oslo and between Denmark's second city, Aarhus and Oslo.
The second would be reserved for charter bookings.
It added that the purchases were expected to raise total passenger volume on the routes to 200,000 from 130,000.
Sun-Air, flying in BA livery, is one of several smaller airlines challenging Scandinavian Airlines System's (SAS) domination of the regional market.
